title: Night Shift: The Closing Window
description: A senior pediatric resident inherits four patients during a night shift. The outgoing framing may be incomplete or wrong. The learner must prioritize, seek disconfirming evidence, stabilize under uncertainty, reassess, communicate, and transfer responsibility safely.

objectives.label: Prioritization
objectives.description: Prioritize competing pediatric patients and reallocate attention when new acuity signals appear.

framework.label: Recognize and manage the acutely ill child
framework.claimBoundary: Curriculum alignment only; one simulation does not establish entrustment.

objectives.label: Diagnostic reasoning
objectives.description: Recognize neonatal shock despite inherited framing, seek disconfirming evidence, and revise the working diagnosis.

framework.label: Clinical reasoning and diagnostic formulation
framework.claimBoundary: Formative mapping; milestone achievement requires longitudinal evidence.

objectives.label: Stabilization under uncertainty
objectives.description: Treat ductal-dependent systemic circulation while maintaining parallel coverage of reversible neonatal threats.

objectives.label: Reassessment and result ownership
objectives.description: Reassess after intervention and close the loop from order placement through review, interpretation, action, or handoff.

framework.label: Monitor response and adjust care
framework.claimBoundary: Local objective mapping, not an official milestone score.

objectives.label: Team communication
objectives.description: Escalate and communicate using graded urgency and closed-loop confirmation.

objectives.label: Safe handoff
objectives.description: Transfer illness severity, active problems, actions, pending work, contingencies, and ownership using I-PASS.

framework.label: Illness severity, patient summary, action list, situation awareness, synthesis
framework.claimBoundary: Structured-field assessment only; not real-world handoff reliability.

signoutOverrides.maya: Six-day-old transferred for slow feeds and tachypnea. Mom is very worried, but the daytime team thought this was mostly feeding adjustment. She can probably be watched overnight.
Six-day-old with poor feeding and tachypnea. The referring team was worried about sepsis, although she has not had a fever. Cultures are not yet drawn.
Six-day-old with poor feeding, tachypnea, and reduced urine output. She needs urgent reassessment; the cause is not clear.

rubric.label: Initial ranking identifies Maya as highest priority
rubric.rationale: The central task is recognizing the highest-risk patient despite inherited framing.
rubric.consequence: Attention may be allocated to lower-acuity patients while shock progresses.

rubric.label: Urgent pages receive a timely clinical response
rubric.rationale: Prioritization is dynamic and includes new escalation signals. Stabilising the highest-acuity patient first is correct; the expectation is that pages are then answered without being forgotten.

rubric.label: Seeks disconfirming evidence early
rubric.rationale: The inherited frame should be actively tested.
rubric.consequence: Diagnostic momentum persists longer than necessary.

rubric.label: Commits to the ductal-dependent systemic circulation mechanism
rubric.rationale: The diagnostic model should explain the perfusion pattern.
rubric.consequence: Management may be correct without demonstrated understanding.

rubric.label: Makes a provisional pathogen-versus-contaminant judgment
rubric.rationale: Uncertainty should be explicit before definitive speciation.
rubric.consequence: The learner waits for the answer rather than reasoning prospectively.

rubric.label: Establishes monitoring and vascular access
rubric.rationale: A crashing neonate requires monitoring and reliable access.
rubric.consequence: Deterioration and complications are managed less safely.

rubric.label: Checks rapid bedside glucose
rubric.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a reversible contributor or mimic.
rubric.consequence: A rapidly reversible threat is not excluded.

rubric.label: Covers sepsis in parallel
rubric.rationale: Cardiac and infectious stabilization may need to proceed in parallel.
rubric.consequence: The pathway reflects premature closure on a cardiac-only explanation.

rubric.label: Prepares airway support before or concurrent with prostaglandin
rubric.rationale: Respiratory support should be immediately available.
rubric.consequence: The treatment complication may occur without readiness.

rubric.label: Starts prostaglandin before severe deterioration
rubric.rationale: Ductal patency is the time-critical bridge.
rubric.consequence: Systemic hypoperfusion progresses and may become incompletely reversible.

rubric.label: Reassesses Maya after prostaglandin
rubric.rationale: Treatment response must be observed rather than assumed.
rubric.consequence: Residual shock or complications may be missed.

rubric.label: Reviews and interprets echocardiography
rubric.rationale: Ordering alone does not demonstrate incorporation of a critical result.

rubric.label: Interprets GBS speciation and CSF findings
rubric.rationale: Organism and CSF findings determine the final pathway.
rubric.consequence: Meningitis classification and treatment planning remain incomplete.

rubric.label: Uses closed-loop cardiac escalation
rubric.consequence: Escalation lacks verified receipt and ownership.

rubric.label: Updates Maya's caregiver
rubric.rationale: Families require an honest explanation during rapid escalation.

rubric.label: Addresses Jamal's caregiver without unnecessary escalation
rubric.rationale: Risk communication should replace reflexive low-value testing.
rubric.consequence: Attention is diverted from higher-acuity patients.

rubric.label: Completes patient-by-patient I-PASS fields
rubric.rationale: Safe transfer requires severity, summary, actions, pending work, and contingencies.
rubric.consequence: The next clinician receives incomplete ownership information.

rubric.label: Assigns ownership of pending work
rubric.rationale: Pending work must be completed or explicitly transferred.
rubric.consequence: Critical results or pages may be lost at shift change.

remediation.title: Prioritization remediation
remediation.instruction: Review the attention ledger and identify where lower-acuity work displaced a higher-acuity need. Repeat with a 60-second re-triage rule after urgent pages.

remediation.title: Diagnostic reasoning remediation
remediation.instruction: Rewrite Maya's problem representation using discriminating findings. State one inherited assumption and one way to falsify it.

remediation.title: Neonatal stabilization remediation
remediation.instruction: Rehearse a parallel first-five-minutes plan: monitor/access, glucose, cultures and sepsis coverage, airway readiness, ductal support, and escalation.

remediation.title: Reassessment and ownership remediation
remediation.instruction: For each intervention, state expected response, reassessment time, and failure threshold. For each test, name who will review and act.

remediation.title: Communication remediation
remediation.instruction: Practice a 20-second graded escalation: assessment, urgency, request, contingency, and read-back.

remediation.title: Handoff remediation
remediation.instruction: Reconstruct one patient using all I-PASS fields, including explicit ownership and a contingency trigger.
